title: The price-drop piggy: refunds for prices that fall after you buy
description: Many shops refund the difference when an item's price drops shortly after you bought it — but only if you ask. Keep the receipts, check the prices for a fortnight, and feed every refund straight into the pig.

body.heading: Set up the system
paragraphs: Give the pig a partner: a receipt envelope that lives beside it. Every receipt for anything over a modest threshold you set — say $20 — goes into the envelope with the date ringed. Beside the pig, keep the list: item, shop, price paid, and the date the shop's price-adjustment window closes (commonly 7–30 days; check each shop's policy and write it down).

Price matching and price adjustment are standing policies at many retailers: if the price falls within the window, the shop refunds the difference to customers who present the receipt. The money is already yours in principle — the system exists to make sure you actually collect it.

body.heading: The Friday five-minute check
paragraphs: Once a week, take five minutes: for each receipt still inside its window, check the item's current price on the shop's site or shelf. Dropped? Take or send the receipt and claim the difference — then put that exact refund amount, in cash or by transfer, into the pig and cross the item off the list.

The amounts are small and that is the point. A $6 refund here and $11 there is a pig that fills itself out of money you had already spent — the purest form of found money, earned by five organised minutes a week.

takeaway: Keep receipts for a fortnight, check each price weekly inside the shop's adjustment window, claim any difference — and feed every refund into the pig.
materials: A piggy bank or savings jar
An envelope or small folder for receipts
A notebook page or phone note for the price-watch list
supervision: No special supervision is required; an adult should handle any claims that involve payment cards or online accounts.
safetyNotes: Never share full card numbers or account passwords when making a claim — a receipt and the item are all a price adjustment should need.
Check each shop's actual policy before relying on a refund window, and do not buy items you do not need just to hunt price drops.
